method.label: Jump six steps at a time

annotationRationale: Repeated substitution produces a six-step recurrence. The values at indices 2, 8, 14, and so on form an arithmetic sequence with common difference 6.
sourceMethod: Followed the second official method, reorganizing its substitutions into a three-step identity and then deriving f(n)=f(n-6)+6.

review.mathCheck: Substitution gives \(f(n)=-f(n-3)+2n-1\) for \(n\ge4\), hence \(f(n)=f(n-6)+6\) for \(n\ge7\). All 336 reductions from 2018 to 2 satisfy that domain restriction, giving \(f(2018)=1+2016=2017\), choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of official solution 20's second approach on page 9. The two displayed identities make the official six-step cancellation reconstructible.
review.annotationCheck: Recurrence manipulation is assessed, and the arithmetic subsequence supplies appropriate supporting knowledge. No induction or additional method is needed.
